_comment: Terminus. The last board in the campaign. Every drone class, every corner type, and the longest route in the game - if anything in your arsenal is dead weight, it shows here. Terminus is the first board with a FORK. alternate_paths carries a second complete road from the same gate to the same exit, and route_weights sends three drones down the long way for every one down the short way. The fork is 10,477 units against the main road's 15,950, so traffic on it arrives sooner and in smaller numbers - it is not a second copy of the same problem, it is a shorter deadline. Closest approach between the two roads away from the shared ends is 250 units, comfortably past twice min_distance_from_path, so both are separately defendable rather than sharing one wall of turrets. The fork only opens once the corridor is fully revealed - acts I and II are one road, acts III and IV are two - because a prefix of a road that is authored to rejoin somewhere else ends in the middle of nowhere.
_premium_cells: Authored premium ground: scarce tiles that make the turret on them better. Placed beside the road at spaced intervals so 'who gets the hill' is a real opening decision.
_breach_paths: Dormant roads, run along whichever lane of the board sits furthest from every existing road. They exist from the first tick of every act so the geometry never appears under a line already built, and so the buildable band includes them - a player can spend slots covering a road that is not open yet. A Breach Borer that survives to its tunnel point opens one for the rest of the act. Placed at the edge because a breach through the middle stole 3-8%% of the main road's build sites and cost Lastlight act III the level.
